clue.text: Trouble with a monkey appearing in Japanese city

parts.note: to trouble someone persistently is to nag them
the saki is a South American monkey

explanation.surface: A troublesome monkey turns up somewhere in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a port city on Kyushu in southern Japan, an example of the category named.

clue.text: How to make one pig or one bird

parts.note: rock is an anagram signal, and shaking up the letters of the bird's name gives the phrase one pig

explanation.surface: A riddle about creating either a pig or a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: 'rock' (shake up) the letters of the bird's name and you get ONE PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock dove, ancestor of town pigeons, is a species of bird found on sea cliffs.

clue.text: New trainee almost senseless kept being unable to figure things out?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the shortened word, keeping it inside them
new signals that the letters of trainee are made into a new arrangement
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: senseless, without feeling, means numb

explanation.surface: A new recruit, nearly unconscious, keeps failing to work things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' scrambles the trainee into INERATE, which has 'kept' the shortened word inside; the question mark flags the pun on figure as calculate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone innumerate lacks basic arithmetic skill, so cannot figure in the sense of calculate; the question mark marks the pun on figure.

clue.text: Awfully grim, what, eh, on Noah's vessel? Flood at maximum here

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it
awfully suggests the letters of grim, what, eh are mangled into a new order

parts.note: Noah built the ark to survive the Flood

explanation.surface: Something grim happens aboard the ark as the Flood reaches its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' scrambles all ten letters of grim, what, eh; 'on' places them above the vessel, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-water mark records the highest level that a flood or tide has reached, so floodwater peaks there.

clue.text: Plans drawn up to provide tinned food

indicators.note: in a down clue, drawn up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: maps are plans of an area

explanation.surface: Plans are prepared for a supply of canned provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn up' looks like preparing plans, but in a down clue it turns MAPS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of canned luncheon meat, a familiar example of food sold in tins.

clue.text: Female anger on account of which the sparks may fly?

definitions.text: on account of which the sparks may fly?

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: An angry woman causes sparks to fly in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparks may fly' suggests a heated argument, but here it is literal: burning wood throws out sparks.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing fire throws off glowing embers, so it is the cause of flying sparks.

clue.text: Adviser to Nero who could create a scene

indicators.note: the letters of a scene can be used to create something new by reordering them

explanation.surface: A counsellor of the emperor Nero who might make a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoic philosopher Seneca was tutor and later political counsellor to the Roman emperor Nero.

clue.text: The French journey on a shallow lake

parts.note: la is a French word for the
to go is to journey
taken as written

explanation.surface: French travellers set off across a shallow stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow salt water separated from the sea by a reef or sandbank.

clue.text: This writer's got a partner diminished in strength

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so this writer is = I'm
someone who has got a partner has been paired off

explanation.surface: A writer finding a partner, only to feel weakened by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired has been damaged or weakened, so it works less well than before.

clue.text: Support of editor acknowledged

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is made of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: An editor's backing was openly recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to the letters running across editoR ACKnowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack is a frame or stand used to hold things up, such as a plate rack or wine rack.

clue.text: Finding it easy to move without picnic basket?

definitions.meaning: free of obstacles, unimpeded in movement
playfully, lacking a hamper, the wicker basket for a picnic

explanation.surface: Moving freely because you've left the picnic basket behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: UN- (without) plus HAMPERED (having a hamper).
explanation.definitionFit: To be unhampered is to be unhindered, so movement comes freely; the joke reads it as lacking a hamper.

clue.text: Newspaper produced by pub in city

indicators.note: the paper sits right next to the pub, as if produced alongside it

parts.note: a bar is a pub or public house
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper comes out of a city pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a short-form British daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a port city in southern Italy, capital of the Apulia region.

clue.text: Two kings who revelled in nonsense?

definitions.text: Two kings who revelled in nonsense?

parts.words: Two kings who revelled in nonsense?
parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings and Lear is Shakespeare's king, together naming a Victorian comic poet

explanation.surface: A pair of monarchs who loved absurdity.
explanation.walkthrough: Two royal names put together give the Victorian poet's full name; King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian poet wrote The Owl and the Pussy-cat and the Book of Nonsense, famous comic verse.

clue.text: See 4
Some elements are rather unusual — with hint of similarity

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of are rather appear in a strange arrangement
a hint of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Some elements are uncommon and share a slight resemblance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ARERATHER to RAREEARTH; 'hint of' gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are the lanthanide metals, a group of chemical elements in the periodic table.

clue.text: Writing "true" tale, I go wrong, penning bit of rubbish

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the rearranged letters hold the extra letter
go wrong signals that the letters of true tale I fall into disorder
a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A writer's true story going awry, full of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wrong' turns TRUETALEI into LITEATURE, which pens R from 'bit of' rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the body of written works, so writing in the collective sense.

clue.text: What avid US magazine reader gets through repeatedly

definitions.text: What avid US magazine reader gets through
definitions.meaning: a keen reader of the American news weekly gets through one issue ... another
again and again, over and over

explanation.surface: A keen American subscriber reads issue after issue.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is the American weekly news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something happening again and again, on many occasions.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
Manage somehow to traverse two lakes as navigator

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across the pair of letters, sitting either side of them
somehow suggests the letters of Manage are put together in some other way

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: An explorer contrives to cross a pair of lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges MANAGE to MAGEAN, which crosses LL by 'to traverse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan was the Portuguese explorer whose expedition first sailed round the world.

clue.text: Source of fruit — one greater after treatment

indicators.note: after treatment the letters of one greater have been worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fruit source that grows better once it has been treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruit grows on this plant, which bears the round orange fruit.

clue.text: Dried fruit is immersed in water

indicators.note: immersed in means plunged inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A dried fruit soaking in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common dried fruit.

clue.text: Equipment required by a capital city

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, such as a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A capital city needs gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Denial of crime — lad is shifty

indicators.note: shifty suggests shifting about, so the letters of crime lad is move into another order

explanation.surface: A suspicious-looking boy denies the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a statement renouncing responsibility, a formal refusal to accept something.

clue.text: Source of power in small room

definitions.meaning: a battery unit that produces electricity
a little room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A power supply kept in a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is both an electrochemical battery unit and a small enclosed chamber for a prisoner or monk.

clue.text: Old Japanese people found in Spain unexpectedly

indicators.note: found in signals that the answer is sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Ancient Japanese folk turn up surprisingly in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across SpAIN Unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ainu are the indigenous people of Hokkaido and northern Japan, predating the Japanese majority.

clue.text: See 4
Up to work

definitions.meaning: until, as far as a certain time
to cultivate soil, as in ploughing a field

explanation.surface: Working until a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: Till means until as a preposition, and as a verb means to prepare and cultivate land.

clue.text: Factory inactive almost — one producing tiles

parts.note: a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: inert means inactive

explanation.surface: A nearly idle factory that makes roof tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiles' suggests roofing, but tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes hats, and tile is old British slang for a hat.

clue.text: The lady's fellow is a jazz musician

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A woman's partner happens to play jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Herman was an American clarinettist and big-band leader in jazz.
